**Pre-market brief — Thursday 2026-11-05**

- **This artifact is a reconstruction.** The 2026-11-05 08:30 ET fire of cron #26 failed on the platform (Token Plan quota) and published nothing.
- The window check resolved this session's scheduled instant to 2026-11-05 08:30:28 ET, so the brief below is rebuilt for **2026-11-05**, not for the day it was written.
- It is point-in-time: every number is what the tape carried before the 09:30 open on Nov 5. What the Nov 5 session actually did is cron #23's business (`daily-briefs/2026-11-05-post-market.md`).

- The pre-market screen is the fleet's own published Nov 5 screen — cron #26b's 10:10:24 ET TradingView pull of the completed 04:00–09:30 ET pre-market session (`preopen-feed/2026-11-05-0830.jsonl`, `daily-briefs/2026-11-05-pre-market-refresh.md`).
- The pre-market high/low on every published name comes from Yahoo's Nov 5 pre-market bars, the prior close and the prior session's move from cron #20's settled EOD file, and the liquidity columns from the same TradingView pull.
- The machine-readable companion for every name in the screen — 708 rows — is `daily-briefs/2026-11-05-pre-market.csv`;
- the tables below are built from that same merged table, so the prose and the CSV cannot disagree.

**Bottom line**

- **The one setup** — APP +28.79% pre-market at 350 against a prior close of 271.8:
- the record Q3 (revenue $2.185B vs $2.078B est, adj EPS $4.30 vs $4.04, Q4 guide $2.365-2.395B) is the only large-cap bid worth chasing into the open.
- It stays a setup while it holds above 350.25 — the pre-market high — and the gap is invalidated on a loss of 309, the pre-market low.
- **The one risk** — the AI complex is being repriced for political reasons, not earnings:
- AMD, QCOM, AVGO, ANET, NET and the memory names are all lower while SMH sits under its 200-day moving average for the first time since May 2025, and Asia has already closed sharply lower (Nikkei {nikkei_chg}, Kospi -5.3% per AP).
- That is a risk to every long, not a single-name gap.
- **The one thing to watch** — the 08:30 ET claims-and-productivity block (initial claims 197K consensus against 194K prior;
- Q3 unit labour costs -0.1% consensus against +1.2% prior) lands with the open, and Cleveland Fed president Beth Hammack speaks at roughly 08:50 ET —
- the hawk who dissented in favour of a hike on Oct 28.

**1. TL;DR**

- The day has one spine:
- **the post-election repricing of the AI build-out, and a violent earnings night underneath it.** Democrats took both chambers on Nov 4, and the tape is trading what that means for data-centre capex.
- The names that need AI silicon are sold; the names that reported are split by their print.

- **AI, semis and memory: a political repricing, not an earnings one.** Leader **AMD -7.52%** —
- **QCOM -13.36%**, **AVGO -4.42%**, **ANET -5.87%**, **NET -5.87%**, **CAMT -4.88%**, **MU -5.37%**, **SNDK -7.17%**, **WDC -6.14%**, **STX -6.54%**, **LITE -5.20%**, **MRVL -5.31%**, **INTC -3.11%**.
- Q3 (Nov 3) was a record — revenue $13.377B (+45% y/y), Data Center $8.546B (+97%), non-GAAP EPS $2.09, Q4 guide ~$17B, 2027 growth >80% —
- and the stock is being marked down on post-election data-centre politics, not the print.
- **AppLovin's record quarter, and the earnings-beat cohort it led.** Leader **APP +28.79%** —
- **SEZL +26.32%**, **LYNX +22.47%**, **U +13.17%**, **WRBY +20.95%**, **TPR +13.32%**, **EPAM +13.72%**, **RPD +13.03%**, **SABR +13.22%**, **PTON +9.16%**, **ALNT +12.27%**, **VCEL +10.53%**, **ULCC +8.04%**. Record Q3:
- revenue $2.185B (+55% y/y) vs $2.078B est, net income $1.439B (+72%), diluted EPS $4.30 vs $4.04, adj EBITDA $1.842B vs $1.732B, FCF $1.4B, Q4 revenue guide $2.365-2.395B vs $2.251B est, buyback raised by $3.2B.
- **The earnings cohort gets marked down.** Leader **MNTN -50.82%** —
- **TRIP -21.18%**, **FOUR -11.76%**, **BROS -14.64%**, **DAVE -12.37%**, **SNAP -10.64%**, **LMAT -6.73%**, **EXPE -9.78%**, **CAVA -8.91%**, **ZG -8.51%**, **MELI -7.98%**, **FICO -7.29%**, **HUBS +3.21%**.
- Cut its 2026 revenue forecast to $311-314M citing problems in its sales team, and named a new chief executive.
- **Small-cap and structural prints at the low end.** Leader **AEHL +103.67%** — **AMTX +38.40%**, **TBI +34.96%**, **ARQ +34.61%**, **ELPW +39.04%**, **LABT +101.15%**, **ZNB +91.32%**, **FLYE +59.99%**.
- No catalyst captured at the Nov 5 checkpoint; the print sits on 4,047,023 pre-market shares (401.2% of ADV).
- **Health-tech and single-name dispersion.** Leader **VCYT -44.00%** —
- **XERS +19.50%**, **IRWD +14.85%**, **ADMA +14.60%**, **RUN +19.34%**, **GROY +16.61%**, **FUN +16.02%**, **BKSY +15.44%**, **AKBA -26.62%**, **KPTI -27.30%**, **ANVS -28.10%**, **ROCK -26.55%**, **GIL -25.51%**, **LZ -24.71%**, **DDD -21.59%**, **TDUP -20.09%**, **PENG -6.93%**, **PH +5.47%**.
- Beat Q3 (adj EPS $0.51 vs $0.41 est, revenue $151.754M vs $147.439M est) but Decipher Prostate volume missed internal expectations;
- FY26 revenue guided to $590-593M from $590-596M, below the $593.894M Street number.

- **The watchlist is quiet.** AAPL +1.26%; MSFT -0.28%; NVDA -2.05%; GOOGL +1.51%; AMZN +2.07%; IWM +0.06% pre-market —
- none of the six names sits in the day's themes, and the file that carries the list was seeded after this fire (see §6).

**2. Theme clusters**

- Levels on every published name:
- **prior close** is the 2026-11-04 settled close, **pre-market last** is the final pre-market print, **PM range** is the 04:00–09:30 ET pre-market low/high, **key level** is the extreme that has to break for the gap to extend (the high on a gap up, the low on a gap down) and **invalidation** is the opposite extreme —
- the level at which the pre-market order failed.
- Market cap is on the **2026-11-04 close basis** throughout — the basis the fleet's screen publishes, because the screen was pulled before the Nov 5 close.
- MELI is absent from cron #20's settled file on both Nov 4 and Nov 5, so its cap is not published rather than guessed.

**8. Macro calendar**

- **Thursday Nov 5 is a Tier 2 day** — claims and productivity, no high-impact release (the fleet's `macro-calendar/2026-11-04-midweek.md`).
- **08:30 ET — Initial Jobless Claims (w/e Oct 31)**, 197K consensus against 194K prior, plus continuing claims and the 4-week average.
- **08:30 ET — Labor Productivity (Q3 prelim)**, +2.9% consensus against +1.4% prior; **Unit Labor Costs (Q3 prelim)**, -0.1% consensus against +1.2% prior.
- **~08:50 ET — Cleveland Fed president Beth Hammack**, and **09:10 ET — Richmond Fed president Thomas Barkin**.
- Hammack dissented in favour of a hike on Oct 28, so her remarks are the hawkish risk in the window.
- **Tomorrow, Friday Nov 6, 08:30 ET — the Employment Situation.** That print is the event this session is positioning around, and it is why the claims block matters.
